clue.text: Opera villain, bass, tucking into beer with full flavour

indicators.note: tucking into means the bass letter is pushed inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
B is the abbreviation for bass in music
rich food or wine has a full flavour

explanation.surface: A bass singer playing the villain is downing a full-bodied beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' is the container signal. Alberich is the villainous dwarf of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberich is the dwarf who steals the Rhinegold in Wagner's Ring cycle, its chief villain.

clue.text: Appreciation of music — loud above all — is a worry

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means the loud letter is placed on top of the rest

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud in music
having an ear for music means appreciating it

explanation.surface: A worried musician finds that loudness dominates their appreciation of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above all' places F on top of EAR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A fear is an anxiety or worry; both work as noun and verb.

clue.text: Put a stop to locating bed in school

indicators.note: the bed is located in the school, so its word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone halts the practice of finding a bed inside a school building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'locating' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to end it decisively, the same as halting it.

clue.text: Line abandoned by fast runners?

indicators.note: the line letter is dropped from the word for fast

parts.note: fleet means swift

explanation.surface: Sprinters leave a starting line behind them as they race off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes L out of FLEET. 'fast runners' reads as one phrase, but 'fast' is FLEET and 'runners?' alone is the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfully, the parts of the body one runs on can be called runners.

clue.text: Introduction of advice to doctors about old source of radiation

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter
the two doctors stand on either side of the letter for old

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree; two doctors give it twice

explanation.surface: Doctors are given early guidance about an outdated radiation source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O between MB and MB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear bomb releases intense radiation when detonated, so it is such a source.

clue.text: Farflung hitchhiker, very keen about Thursday

indicators.note: the word for very keen goes around the short form of the weekday

parts.note: ardent means passionate or very keen
THUR is a short form of Thursday

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic traveller thumbs a lift on a Thursday to somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The hero of Douglas Adams's The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy is flung across the universe on a Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Adams character travels across the galaxy by thumbing lifts on spaceships.

clue.text: Very familiar swindle, netting old money repeatedly

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so the swindle surrounds the rest

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: the money letter is given twice

explanation.surface: A well-worn scam keeps catching out people of old-fashioned wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' puts OMM (O, then 'repeatedly' doubling M) inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common is ordinary and widely known, hence very familiar.

clue.text: Ocean waste down

definitions.meaning: to squander money is to spend it freely

explanation.surface: An ocean is being wasted away.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the blue for the sea, to blow money, and low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers the sea, squandering cash, and being depressed.

clue.text: Author runs into school in pursuit of box

indicators.note: following behind, so the school part comes after the box

parts.note: a chest is a large box

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the name of the school

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A writer dashes into school to chase after a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal and 'in pursuit of' places the school part after the box. Eton is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the English writer of the Father Brown stories.

clue.text: Clandestine team mostly concealed within group

indicators.note: the shortened team sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A covert team operates mostly hidden inside a larger group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the team word; 'concealed within' puts the rest inside the group word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clandestine is kept hidden, which is a synonym of secret.

clue.text: Little fellow's tense, busy sound, drilling into mausoleum

indicators.note: the tense letter and busy sound bore inside the tomb

parts.note: a mausoleum is a large tomb
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the hum of activity is a busy sound

explanation.surface: A small man is stressed by noisy drilling into a mausoleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drilling into' is the container signal. The answer is the tiny hero of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: The folklore character is no bigger than his father's thumb, a tiny fellow.

clue.text: Political commentaries dismissing politician's foremost misdemeanours

indicators.note: dismissing means one letter is sent away from the commentaries

parts.note: spin is political slanting of news; plural spins

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Political spin removes any mention of a politician's misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes P ('foremost' of politician's) from SPINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sins are wrongdoings, as are misdemeanours.

clue.text: Closely follow sister with lamp at war

indicators.note: things at war are in conflict and disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A nurse sister follows closely with a lamp in wartime, like Florence Nightingale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at war' rearranges SISTER and LAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To slipstream is to travel just behind another vehicle in its air current, following closely.

clue.text: Inspirational fountain (hope prince is upset)

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prince's hope for an inspiring fountain has been dashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HOPE and PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocrene is the spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses, a source of poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Foodstuff clearly behind answer in the dictionary?

parts.note: past means behind or beyond

explanation.surface: A food item's entry comes well after the answer in a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dictionary?' adds a joke: the word sits in P, well past the A section of a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple food, so a foodstuff.

clue.text: I live with banishment after translating novella

indicators.note: translating turns the words into another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exile's life story is rendered from another language into a short novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' rearranges I LIVE and BANISHMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells's The Invisible Man is a short novel, often called a novella.

clue.text: Book following volume one assessed as 'offered pulsating stuff'

indicators.note: the book letter comes after the volume and one letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rated means judged or assessed

explanation.surface: A reviewer judges a book's opening volume to be throbbing with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places B after VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that vibrated gave off pulsing motion, a playful paraphrase of the definition.

clue.text: Computer program betrayed British Nobel physicist

parts.note: an app is a computer application
to let on is to reveal a secret, betraying it

explanation.surface: Some software has given away the secrets of a prize-winning British scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Appleton won the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the ionosphere.

clue.text: Men (with two women) squared off for a battle here

definitions.text: Men (with two women) squared off for a battle here

parts.words: Men (with two women) squared off for a battle here
parts.note: chessmen, including two queens, face each other across a squared board for a game of war

explanation.surface: Two women join men squaring up for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'men' are chess pieces, the 'two women' the queens, and 'squared' the chequered pattern of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces fight their mock war on this chequered board.

clue.text: Lay into poor actor: "Simply half-cut"

parts.note: a ham is an over-acting performer

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away

parts.note: merely means simply

explanation.surface: A critic savages a bad actor who was simply drunk on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' cuts MERELY to MER; 'half-cut' looks like a slang word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is to attack them hard, in words or blows, as in to pound them.

clue.text: Weapon threat? Good to replace nuclear

indicators.note: one letter is swapped in for another in the word for threat

parts.note: a danger is a threat

explanation.surface: A weapons threat is lessened by swapping nuclear arms for something better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps G in for N in DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger is a short stabbing blade, a weapon.

clue.text: You might assume it's occurred in faulty posting

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words faulty posting, across the gap

parts.note: a badly keyed message would contain a slip of the keys

explanation.surface: Reading a badly worded post, you might guess a slip has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters spanning the two words. The definition is playful: a keyed slip is what you would assume had happened in a faulty posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is the slip a reader suspects on spotting an error in text.

clue.text: Know-it-all in America starts to spot many associations with 'Flying Stars'?

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words give their opening letters
flying means scattering in all directions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smug American spots many connections with a team called the Flying Stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives SMA; 'Flying' rearranges STARS to RTASS. The Flying Stars is a Father Brown story by Chesterton (9 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Smartass is American slang for a smug person who thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Notice picked up in Hayling Island

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read from the bottom upward
the letters are found inside the island's name

explanation.surface: A notice was collected on Hayling Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes NGIS from HaylING ISland, and 'picked up' turns it upward. Hayling Island is off the south coast of England, in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a posted notice.

clue.text: Government set to offload first growth area

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for set is dropped

parts.note: to set is to harden, like concrete

explanation.surface: The government plans to sell off its leading growth region first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to offload first' trims HARDEN to ARDEN. 'growth area' sounds economic but means where plants grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot where plants are grown.

clue.text: Service just on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word for just is said aloud

parts.note: right means just or fair

explanation.surface: A church service broadcast only on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' signals the sound of RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a religious ceremony, a church service.

clue.text: Foreign articles about blow to Attorney General (a keen lawyer)

indicators.note: the two foreign articles go on either side of the rest

parts.note: le is the French definite article; two of them give it twice
a gale is a strong blow of wind

explanation.surface: Overseas newspaper articles describe a storm hitting the Attorney General.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sends the two French articles round the rest; 'Foreign articles' are French 'le'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal eagle is an idiom for a sharp, eager lawyer.

clue.text: Plunder brought back — it's something to work with

indicators.note: brought back means the word for plunder is read backwards

parts.note: loot means plunder

explanation.surface: A thief returns stolen goods, calling it something useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns LOOT around.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement for doing a job is a piece of equipment.
